findings.amendment: Smallest safe fix is documentation plus one line of carry-over: in the --out-dir reuse branch (scripts/capture.mjs:408-427), before deleting the prior receipt.json, read its `required_coverage` and seed the new receipt with it; and reword README.md:9/67/235 and SKILL.md:71 from 'never quietly narrowed' to 'the requirement is stored on that receipt and survives re-capture into the same out-dir; a fresh out-dir starts with no requirement, so the caller must pass --require again'. If the carry-over is judged out of scope for 0.2.0, ship the wording change alone — but the claim as written must not go public unqualified.
findings.failure_mode: The sticky coverage requirement — the headline 0.2.0 feature — lives only inside the receipt it guards, and the documented re-capture path deletes that receipt. OBSERVED (executed against docs/demo/fixed served on 127.0.0.1:9232): a run captured at desktop+mobile, all 8 PNGs attested, then `check --require 'desktop:*,mobile:*'` -> exit 0 and `required_coverage: ['desktop:*','mobile:*']` written to the receipt; a plain `check` still enforced it. Then re-running capture into the SAME --out-dir with `--viewports desktop=1280x800 --tabs Overview --screenshot-mode viewport` produced `required_coverage: None`, and after one attestation a plain `check` returned `screenshots: 1, attested: 1, findings: 0 / OK ...` exit 0. Mobile was never captured and nothing in the receipt or the check output records that a mobile requirement ever existed. README.md:67 ('a matrix can be widened but never quietly narrowed'), README.md:9 ('so a narrower re-capture cannot hide a defect') and the whole of walkthrough section 5 ('Capturing less does not help either') are therefore false for the most ordinary narrowing action an agent can take. Note README.md:207 explicitly tells the reader that re-running capture into the same directory is a normal thing to do.

findings.amendment: Accept optional dimensions in the requirement grammar (`mobile:Overview@390x844`) and match them against `shot.viewport.width/height`; at minimum, have `check` print each satisfied requirement with the dimensions that satisfied it (e.g. `COVERAGE: mobile:Overview -> 1280x800`) so a reader can see a mislabelled viewport, and state in README.md:67 that `--require` matches viewport names, not sizes.
findings.failure_mode: `--require` is satisfied by the *label* the capturing agent chose for a viewport, not by the dimensions it actually rendered at, even though the receipt already stores width and height on every shot. OBSERVED (executed against the DEFECTIVE docs/demo page on 127.0.0.1:9231): `--viewports 'desktop=1280x800,mobile=1280x800' --tabs 'Overview,Orders'` produced `status: capture_complete_requires_human_inspection`, `findings: []`, and shots recorded as [('desktop',1280),('desktop',1280),('mobile',1280),('mobile',1280)]. After attesting all four, `check --require 'desktop:Overview,desktop:Orders,mobile:Overview,mobile:Orders'` returned `screenshots: 4, attested: 4, findings: 0 / OK: every screenshot inspected against its current bytes, nothing failed`, exit 0. The full declared matrix reports satisfied while the 390px render — the only viewport in which the clipped_content defect this repo is built around exists — was never taken. This defeats the same class of narrowing that finding 1 covers, without touching the receipt at all, and it is the failure the prior Opus review's amendment was meant to close.

findings.amendment: Before flipping: run a history-wide scan and either confirm clean or squash/rewrite. Do not treat this review as covering it — this review covers commit 142c940 only.
findings.failure_mode: Flipping the repo public exposes every commit ever made, not the tip tree. All three reviews (Luna, Opus, this one) were given a `git archive` of a single commit, so no reviewer has ever examined history. The tip tree is clean — I found no emails, hostnames, tailnet names, home paths, credentials, tokens, browser profiles, internal ports, wrapper scripts or custom User-Agent strings anywhere outside the deliberate 'Karina Qian' (LICENSE, SKILL.md) and 'ykq' (README clone URL); docs/reviews scratch paths are already replaced with `<packet>`/`<scratch>`; the committed example receipts carry `out_dir: /tmp/demo/run-N`, `url: http://127.0.0.1:893N/`, `chrome: null`, `user_agent: null`; the 16 committed PNGs contain only IHDR/IDAT/IEND chunks (no tEXt/iTXt/eXIf). But the history predates the redaction work described in the CHANGELOG, and earlier receipts embedded ABSOLUTE paths (schema 3, per the Luna finding), which is precisely the class of leak that would have carried the owner's real machine paths. Luna asked this question explicitly and CHANGELOG.md:20's 'Owner decisions on reviewer questions' does not record an answer.

findings.amendment: Wrap the `withReceiptLock` call at scripts/capture.mjs:323 in try/catch; on EACCES/EROFS/EPERM emit `error: cannot record --require on a read-only receipt: <path>` and continue enforcing the union in memory for this invocation, exiting with the normal gate code rather than crashing.
findings.failure_mode: `check --require` is a mutating operation, and it has no error handling for an unwritable location. OBSERVED: `chmod -w` on a copied run directory, then `check receipt.json --require 'tablet:Overview'` printed a raw Node stack trace (`Error: EACCES: permission denied, open '.../receipt.json.lock'` plus five `at ...` frames exposing absolute filesystem paths) and exited **1**. Exit 1 is documented at README.md:250 as 'Capture failed (receipt records the error)', so a CI gate branching on the exit code misreports a permissions problem as a failed browser capture, and tests/test_capture.sh's own invariant ('usage errors exit 64 without stack traces', line 100) is violated. This directly undercuts README.md:273's advertised workflow — 'A run directory can be copied or uploaded and checked elsewhere' — since archived/restored evidence directories are commonly read-only. It fails closed (nonzero), so no bad work passes; the defect is the wrong error class and the stack trace on a first public release.
findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:322-334 (check writes required_coverage) via withReceiptLock at scripts/capture.mjs:230-251; exit-code table at README.md:248-255

owner_questions: Has anyone scanned the pre-0.2.0 git history for secrets, absolute home paths, machine names and internal hostnames? Luna asked this in docs/reviews/2026-09-01-luna/review.json:102 and CHANGELOG.md:20 records no answer. If the answer is no, this is the one item I would not flip without.

Is required_coverage meant to be a durable policy for a *task* (in which case it needs to live outside the receipt, e.g. a --coverage-file or a CI-side declaration) or merely a convenience flag for a *single receipt*? The README currently promises the former and the code implements the latter; which one do you want 0.2.0 to ship?

Do you want `check` to remain a mutating command? A verification gate that writes to the evidence it is verifying is surprising, breaks on read-only evidence archives, and means `check` cannot be safely run against committed example receipts with --require. An alternative is to make --require purely in-memory and require CI to pass it every time.

README.md:203 links to commit c78fd09 via the relative path `../../commit/c78fd09`. Will that commit still be reachable after the flip (i.e. is history being preserved rather than squashed)? If you squash for the history reasons above, that link and the 'both records are in git history' claim both break.

`out_dir` is now purely informational under schema 4 and is the only unavoidable local-path disclosure in a shared receipt. Do you want a flag to suppress it, or is the documented disclosure at README.md:246/273 sufficient for your users?
The Opus review's suggestion to reject byte-identical notes across screenshots was not implemented. Deliberate deferral (in which case it should appear in the CHANGELOG) or an oversight?
package.json sets "private": true. Intentional npm-publish guard for a repo that is going public, or a leftover you want removed alongside the version bump?
